$comment: The single source for response headers. vercel.ts turns these into the deploy config, and scripts/check-export.mjs asserts against the same list, so the guard cannot drift from what is actually served.

rules.$comment: Scoped to the docs tree rather than every .md path, because a header rule cannot be conditioned on response status: a catch-all stamped text/markdown onto the HTML 404 body served for any invented .md address. The pattern is deliberately /(docs.*) and not /docs/(.*), because the index mirror is written to public/docs.md, outside the public/docs directory.

The mirrors are near-verbatim duplicates of pages that are themselves indexable, so they name the HTML page as canonical. A markdown file cannot carry a rel=canonical link element, and this header is the documented equivalent for a non-HTML resource. :path+ requires at least one segment, which keeps this rule disjoint from the /docs.md rule below rather than relying on which of two matching rules wins.

Every app route exports a sibling .txt holding the page's full React payload, which the client router prefetches. They cannot be removed without breaking client-side navigation, and they carry no robots signal of their own, so they are a parallel indexable copy of the whole site. The negative lookahead spares llms.txt and llms-full.txt, which exist to be retrieved; scripts/check-export.mjs compiles this exact pattern and asserts that split over the real exported file set.

A static export cannot return 404 for the not-found route's own file, so it answers 200. Next injects its own noindex on the rendered page; this repeats it at the transport layer, where a crawler reads it without parsing the body.

A megabyte of JSON holding the full text of every docs page. It has to stay public for the docs search to work, but it is a third copy of the corpus after the HTML and the mirrors, so it is kept out of the index.
